title: fix: stop Open WebUI injecting builtin tools into every chat
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Sets `DEFAULT_MODEL_METADATA={"capabilities":{"builtin_tools":false}}`. Open WebUI appends its builtin tool specs to every request from its UI unless the model says otherwise; connection-fetched models have no `model` row, so the global default is the only lever (`utils/models.py` applies it to them wholesale).
- Fixes managed agents and community models that reject a `tools` field 400-ing on every chat, without touching gen.
- The Pollinations MCP server is unaffected — it arrives via the request body, so it stays opt-in per chat.
- Both live config rows (`openwebui`, `openwebui_staging`) were updated directly; the env var is inert on a booted DB because `Config.seed_defaults` only inserts missing keys. Verified live: all 425 models on production now report `builtin_tools: false`, retroactively for existing chats and users (`models.base_models_cache` is false and `Config.get_many` reads per request).
- README: documents the above and corrects a stale claim that the database is Neon.

Upstream confirms this is the intended fix — open-webui/open-webui#28540 was closed as already-satisfied by `DEFAULT_MODEL_METADATA`, and #26823 reports the same defaulting bug.

gist.headline: Tools stay in their garden
gist.blurb: Open WebUI has stopped packing builtin tools into every single chat like an overprepared picnic basket. Models that prefer a tool-free request can now simply answer the question.
gist.summary: Configured Open WebUI's default model metadata with `capabilities.builtin_tools: false`, preventing its UI from attaching builtin tool specifications to all 425 production models while leaving Pollinations MCP tools opt-in per request.
gist.impact: Managed agents and community models that reject a `tools` field can now chat through Open WebUI without recurring 400 errors, while MCP-enabled chats keep working when users explicitly send those tools.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy Open WebUI-style retro chat terminal is tidily sorting a pile of unused tool cards into a garden shed instead of adding them to every message. Polli, wearing a tiny gardener apron, checks that the chat path is clear; a small code-plant and flowers reinforce that tools remain available when deliberately chosen.
